items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: Buddy Johnson. Buddy Johnson. Buddy Johnson. And Galle was the banjo.

ctx.x: Anyway, I was going to ask some more about the Sam Morgan Band. Who else was in it, if you remember the other men at that time?

Yeah, well, Sam Morgan Band, it was Sam playing trumpet, Yank playing trombone, and his brother used to play trombone too. Buddy. Buddy Johnson. Buddy Johnson. Buddy Johnson. And Galle was the banjo. And Sam Morgan trumpet. Did they have a bass player then, before you? Yes, they had a bass player before me at that time. And I'll finish telling you about the other man or two, what Sam Morgan had. For Alfred Williams. Mm-hmm. He had Alfred playing drums.
And Joe Watson playing clarinet. You heard about Joe Watson playing clarinet. Did they have a bass player then?

items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: I got my Uncle B's violin. Because he had quit playing that time.

ctx.x: I think it's the absence of you told me. Yeah. When you came to New Orleans in New York, were you looking for a music job or why did you come to New Orleans?

No I come here to live then. And we got together Sam Morgan and I got together right at that time you see. And we had a little six piece band around then. What were you playing then? I was playing violin. Violin. Uh huh. And it's a little while after I, I wasn't finished growing at the time. And just about the time I was getting big enough to, that I could get tall enough to reach a bass you know? And then I got my Uncle B's violin. Because he had quit playing that time.
